newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks roar, then fade on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks roar, then fade on profit-taking.

text.p: Mexico's stock market closed weaker Wednesday, as an early rally to historic highs fizzled amid profit-taking.
The stock market hit a new intraday record soon after opening on strong foreign buying, when the main index rose 0.60 percent, or 20.68 points, to 3,454.31 points
But the market started to slide during the day, and its main index closed down 0.667 percent, or 22.91 points, to 3,410.84 points.
"It's only a breather. The market feels positive and in the short term it could hit 3,500," said one trader.
The market has been given a boost of energy by recent data showing the economy is steaming ahead. In the second quarter gross domestic product grew by 7.2 percent.
The market was also cheered by rumours that President Ernesto Zedillo may announce measures to spur growth when he gives his annual state of the union address Sunday.
Market players are looking forward to better second-quarter growth in earnings.
On Tuesday, the market's main index closed 2.281 percent or 76.58 points higher, at a record 3,433.75 points. Construction stocks were big gainers, as was cement producer Cemex.
On Wednesday, the builders continued to shine. Among the biggest gainers on the day was construction company Tribasa, up 1.0 peso (13 cents) to 19.80 pesos ($2.64).
Construction company Bufete CPO also rose, gaining 2.1 pesos (28 cents) to 45.60 pesos ($6.08).
Among the biggest losers was Grupo Financiero Abaco A, down 33 centavos (4 cents) to 2.80 pesos (37 cents).
Volume was 157,970,333. There were 36 stocks that gained, 58 that declined and 24 that were unchanged.
